question: During a hysterectomy, a surgeon is ligating the uterine artery at the level of the internal os. Which adjacent structure is at greatest risk of inadvertent injury at this point?

answers.text: Obturator nerve, running along the lateral pelvic wall

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The obturator nerve runs on the lateral pelvic wall and is not immediately adjacent to the uterine artery at the internal os.

answers.text: Ureter, which crosses beneath the uterine artery approximately 1.5 cm lateral to the cervix

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct! The ureter passes 1–1.5 cm lateral to the cervix and crosses UNDER the uterine artery — remembered as 'water under the bridge'. This is the most common serious complication of hysterectomy.

answers.text: Round ligament, which lies anterior to the fallopian tube

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The round ligament is an anterior structure and is not at immediate risk during uterine artery ligation near the cervix.

answers.text: Internal iliac vein, directly posterior to the uterine artery

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: The internal iliac vein is more lateral and posterior. While vascular injury is possible, the ureter is the canonical anatomical trap in this location.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the mnemonic 'water under the bridge': the ureter (water) passes beneath the uterine artery (bridge) ~1.5 cm lateral to the cervix.
Excellent! 'Water under the bridge' — the ureter runs under the uterine artery. This is the most important single anatomical fact in pelvic surgery.
